newsitem.title: UK: Utd News set for Westcountry TV takeover.
newsitem.headline: Utd News set for Westcountry TV takeover.

text.p: Britain's United News and Media is poised to extend its UK commercial television operations by taking over privately-owned Westcountry Television, sources close to the negotiations said on Thursday.
United News and Westcountry both declined to comment but the sources said that an announcement was likely next week.
"United News have completed their due diligence and are now haggling over price," said one media industry source.
"It's just a question of when the puff of white smoke will appear," he added. Analysts said they believed the price was likely to be in the 75-85 million stg range.
But one source said that United News chief executive Clive Hollick was likely to try to negotiate the price down to a level of around 65 million stg.

Westcountry, which had been considering a flotation, last year reported profits of five million stg on 38 million turnover and has a potential audience of two million in the southwestern corner of England.

United News operates commercial television (ITV) licences in southern England through its Meridian unit and eastern England where it runs Anglia TV. Last month it took a 20 percent stake in HTV, the ITV company for Wales and west England.

Speculation that United News was planning a fresh acquisition grew on Thursday when it said it was raising 180 million stg through an issue of convertible bonds. United recently paid 592 million stg for exhibitions group Blenheim.

Analyst Anthony de Larrinaga of Panmure Gordon put a price tag of 85 million stg on Westcountry but said that this was based on a calculation that it would be able to negotiate a cut in its annual franchise payments from 1999.
De Larrinaga said that he calculated that Westcountry should be able to secure a reduction in payments from nine million stg in 1998 to around 4.5 million the following year.
The acquisition of Westcountry would make it more likely that United would eventually make a full bid for its western neighbour HTV.
United said last month that it regarded the stake as an investment and had no plans to bid for the rest of the capital of HTV, valued at around 310 million stg.
